source.title: Antrim County Council printed minutes, 1920-21, pp. 1-2, minute 7717: the members returned at the triennial election of county councillors, June 1920 (PRONI LA/1/2/GB/21)
source.publisher: Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (Antrim County Council records)
source.check: the 21 members returned for the five electoral areas, as the printed minute lists them (owner's PRONI photographs, transcribed 11 Nov 2026); the votes and any unsuccessful candidates are not in the minute

note: Proportional representation (single transferable vote) under the Local Government (Ireland) Act 1919: the first county council election in the five electoral areas that replaced the county electoral divisions of 1899, 21 seats. The members are as the council's minute of its first meeting lists them; the votes are not yet found in the sources searched. Poll date: Thursday 3 June 1920, as given by Wikipedia's article on the election (citing the Belfast News-Letter); the minute does not give it, and it is still to be confirmed from a newspaper. The minute also records the chairmen of the rural district councils, who sat ex officio, and the co-opted members; they were not elected and are not listed here.
